comparison.objective: Isolate an HVAC unit by removing and reversing a pull-out disconnect, closing its cover, and applying a padlock; candidate tunes and locks a robot-axis damper for repeatable non-bottoming stops.
comparison.physical_skill: Disconnect task combines cover support, forceful block extraction, 180-degree reorientation and reinsertion, shackle insertion, and lock latching. Candidate combines hex-key insertion, setscrew torque control, fine collar rotation under counterhold, and iterative physical test cycling.
comparison.success_condition: Disconnect success requires the selected block seated OFF, cover shut, padlock latched through the tab, a 20 N release test passed, and the other disconnect untouched. Candidate requires two acceptable impact cycles, stroke at or below 12 mm, no hard-stop strike, rebound, overload, or drift, and a physically retained collar.
comparison.reason: Both include insertion and a locking action, but their central tested abilities are different: establishing and mechanically verifying electrical lockout versus adjusting a continuous damping parameter and judging repeated dynamic response. Candidate still lacks numeric rebound, overload, witness-torque, and drift tolerances; this weakens its rubric completeness but does not make it a duplicate of the discrete pull-out-and-padlock sequence.
